chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

He said: Al-Qabalah (leasing) is that you come to the barren land, so you accept it from its owners for twenty years, or less than that or more, so you cultivate it and pay what is due upon it, so there is no problem with it.

key_terms.الْقَبَالَةُ: Leasing or contracting for land cultivation
key_terms.فَلَا بَأْسَ بِهِ: So there is no problem with it (permissible)

ai.seo_question: What is the definition and ruling of Al-Qabalah (land leasing) in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi defines 'Al-Qabalah' as a leasehold agreement where barren land is reclaimed and cultivated in exchange for a fixed duration and tax payment, reflecting the early Shia juristic emphasis on agricultural development and land reclamation. It underscores the practical application of property rights in Shia fiqh, allowing flexible lease terms to incentivize productivity and ensure state revenue through dues.
